question: Should read-scoped `openclaw health` include auth/provider drift path names while keeping fingerprints and detailed disk-read errors admin-only?
rationale: The code can mechanically avoid observed-read side effects, but the auth-adjacent visibility boundary and cache-hit IO cost are product/operations choices that CI cannot settle.

options.title: Keep Read-Scoped Drift Paths
options.body: After the side-effect-free read fix, land with path names visible to `operator.read` callers and sensitive fingerprints/errors restricted to admin scope.

options.title: Make Runtime Config Drift Admin-Only
options.body: Restrict the new `runtimeConfig` health block to admin-scoped callers if path names are considered sensitive in ordinary health output.

options.title: Bundle With Restart Policy
options.body: Pause this diagnostic until maintainers decide whether it must land together with the companion hot-mode restart policy PR.

recommendation.title: Keep Read-Scoped Drift Paths
recommendation.body: After the side-effect-free read fix, land with path names visible to `operator.read` callers and sensitive fingerprints/errors restricted to admin scope.
